latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Expansion of malignant lymphoid precursor cells in marrow, blood, lymphoid tissue, and extramedullary sites. Drives blast fraction, hyperleukocytosis or leukopenia patterns, organ infiltration, tumor lysis pressure, and relapse pressure.

Developmental arrest of B- or T-lineage precursors creates sustained blast accumulation and failure to generate mature functional lymphoid cells. This is the core ALL geometry; lineage and genotype modulate therapy response but are not separate first-layer constraints here.

Blast replacement of marrow niches suppresses erythropoiesis, megakaryopoiesis, and granulopoiesis, producing anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, fatigue, pallor, bleeding, and infection susceptibility.

Lymphoblasts infiltrate lymph nodes, spleen, liver, mediastinum, skin, bone, testis, kidney, or other tissues. Produces lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, compressive mediastinal symptoms, cholestasis, renal injury, and tissue-specific mimicry.

Lymphoblasts can seed leptomeninges, cranial nerves, optic/retinal compartments, or brain/spinal spaces. CNS involvement may be occult at presentation and becomes a relapse sanctuary without CNS-directed therapy.

High circulating lymphoblast count increases blood viscosity, endothelial adhesion, and microvascular obstruction, especially in CNS, retina, lung, kidney, and heart. Less common than AML leukostasis at the same WBC but clinically critical when present.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: High cell-turnover and tumor lysis pressure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: High proliferative burden and cytotoxic therapy release uric acid, potassium, phosphate, and nucleic acids, causing metabolic tumor lysis, AKI, seizure, arrhythmia, dialysis need, and early death.

Leukemic and stromal cytokines can drive bone pain, osteopenia, lytic lesions, pathologic fracture risk, and hypercalcemia with renal injury. This is uncommon but important, especially in children and relapsed disease.

Portal, sinusoidal, parenchymal, or biliary infiltration by lymphoblasts can create cholestatic jaundice, hepatomegaly, high bilirubin, and obstructive-pattern enzymes without ordinary gallstone obstruction.

Disease-related neutropenia, mucosal barrier injury, corticosteroids, intensive chemotherapy, asparaginase, central lines, and prolonged cytopenias increase bacterial, fungal, and viral infection risk; infection can mimic or compound leukemia fever.

Circulating lymphoblast percentage reflects marrow release and blood burden when blasts spill into blood.
Absolute circulating blast count combines WBC and blast fraction and tracks leukostasis/TLS pressure.
ALL can present with leukopenia, normal WBC, leukocytosis, or extreme hyperleukocytosis.
High proliferation, tissue injury, and cell turnover elevate LDH.
Blast occupation of marrow suppresses normal hematopoiesis.
Anemia is common from impaired erythropoiesis, bleeding, inflammation, and treatment.
Thrombocytopenia produces petechiae, bruising, mucosal bleeding, and transfusion need.
Granulopoiesis suppression creates neutropenia even when total WBC is high.
Hypoproliferative marrow failure causes an inappropriately low reticulocyte production response despite anemia.
Anemia and systemic illness drive fatigue and weakness.
Pallor tracks clinically visible anemia.
Severe thrombocytopenia and mucosal injury increase major bleeding risk.
Marrow failure predisposes to febrile neutropenia before and during therapy.
Infection and leukemia cytokines cause fever.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Bleeding hazard rises with severe thrombocytopenia.
Intracranial hemorrhage is a catastrophic subset of major bleeding.
Febrile neutropenia accelerates when ANC is low.
Some febrile neutropenia progresses to sepsis or septic shock.
High WBC is an imperfect but clinically important leukostasis risk marker.
Absolute blast burden is closer to leukostasis mechanism than total WBC.
Pulmonary leukostasis can progress to respiratory failure.
LDH marks high turnover and TLS risk.
Uric acid nephropathy contributes to AKI.
Hypercalcemia causes dehydration/nephrocalcinosis risk, while TLS hypocalcemia marks severe metabolic disturbance.
More extensive lytic disease increases fracture risk.
Clinical TLS frequently injures kidney through uric acid, phosphate, volume, and shock pathways.
Direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase often move together in cholestatic infiltration.
Infection and sterile leukemia inflammation often move CRP and fever together, but loosely.
Leukostasis can cause fatal CNS, pulmonary, cardiac, or renal complications.
Sepsis is a dominant early and treatment-course mortality path.
Intracranial hemorrhage has high fatality.
TLS increases mortality through arrhythmia, AKI, seizure, and shock.
Respiratory failure increases short-term death hazard.
Pathologic fracture itself is rarely the direct cause of death but signals severe skeletal disease, immobility, and treatment complexity.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hydroxyurea can temporarily lower WBC/blast burden while definitive ALL therapy and stabilization are arranged.
Rapid cytoreduction without TLS prophylaxis can worsen metabolic collapse.

side_effects.interpretation: Cytoreduction can precipitate TLS.
Additional marrow suppression can deepen neutropenia.

treatments.context_specific_role: Short-term debulking vector for hyperleukocytic or rapidly rising ALL while diagnosis, TLS prevention, and definitive regimen planning proceed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Apheresis requires vascular access, staffing, anticoagulation tolerance, and hemodynamic stability.
Line placement and anticoagulation become riskier with bleeding pressure.

side_effects.interpretation: Central access and anticoagulation can increase bleeding risk.
Citrate exposure can lower calcium.

treatments.context_specific_role: Temporary debulking for symptomatic leukostasis; must be paired with cytoreductive or definitive leukemia therapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroids can rapidly lyse lymphoblasts and trigger TLS.
Steroids can mask fever and worsen uncontrolled infection.

side_effects.interpretation: Steroid cytoreduction can trigger TLS.
Immunosuppression and fever masking can increase infection risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapid lymphoblast-sensitive vector field used in induction/prephase and some bridging contexts; downstream effects depend on TLS and infection controls.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Frailty, organ failure, pregnancy, cardiac dysfunction, or goals may limit intensive induction.
Rapid blast kill without TLS control is dangerous.
Vincristine, anthracycline, azoles, and asparaginase toxicity/dosing are altered by hepatic dysfunction.
Pancreatitis, thrombosis, hepatic injury, or allergy can limit asparaginase exposure.

side_effects.interpretation: Expected induction aplasia.
Treatment aplasia creates high febrile neutropenia risk.
Aplasia and mucositis amplify bleeding risk.
Profound immunosuppression can lead to sepsis.

treatments.context_specific_role: Core disease-eradicating vector field for fit patients; benefit emerges from blast reduction, marrow recovery, CNS control, and remission depth.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CNS disease increases the value of CNS-directed therapy.
Lumbar puncture is riskier with severe thrombocytopenia or coagulopathy.

side_effects.interpretation: Post-lumbar-puncture or chemical meningitis symptoms can occur.
Procedure bleeding risk depends on platelet/coagulation context.

treatments.context_specific_role: CNS sanctuary vector field; effect is not replaceable by ordinary systemic therapy alone.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: TKI benefit depends on BCR-ABL1 signaling context.
Hepatic dysfunction and drug interactions affect TKI exposure and toxicity.

side_effects.interpretation: TKIs can cause liver enzyme elevation or interaction toxicity.
Myelosuppression can worsen cytopenia.

treatments.context_specific_role: BCR-ABL1 signaling vector modifier when the target context is present.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CD19-negative or dim disease will not respond adequately.
High burden raises cytokine-release and neurologic toxicity risk.

side_effects.interpretation: Cytokine release can cause fever.
Immune effector neurotoxicity can occur.

treatments.context_specific_role: CD19-directed immune vector field for MRD persistence, relapse/refractory disease, or selected chemotherapy-sparing contexts.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CD22 target expression is required.
Veno-occlusive/sinusoidal obstruction and hepatic injury risk rise with hepatic vulnerability.

side_effects.interpretation: Hepatic sinusoidal injury risk.
Cytopenias can worsen.

treatments.context_specific_role: CD22-directed cytotoxic vector field when target expression and hepatic context permit.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CD19-negative disease cannot be targeted.
Severe infection can make lymphodepletion/CAR-T unsafe.
High tumor burden raises CRS and ICANS risk.

side_effects.interpretation: CRS commonly causes fever.
Severe CRS can cause hypotension.
ICANS neurotoxicity can cause encephalopathy, aphasia, or seizure.

treatments.context_specific_role: Delayed but potent CD19-directed cellular vector field for relapsed/refractory or selected high-risk disease.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Persistent MRD or high relapse pressure increases value of graft-versus-leukemia control.
Uncontrolled infection strongly raises transplant-related mortality.
Frailty and organ dysfunction reduce transplant feasibility.

side_effects.interpretation: Conditioning and immunosuppression increase infection risk.
Sinusoidal obstruction, GVHD, or drug injury can affect liver.
Transplant aplasia and mucositis increase bleeding risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Long-horizon relapse-pressure reshaping through graft-versus-leukemia immunity, with substantial treatment-related hazard.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High TLS risk increases the value of hydration, monitoring, and urate lowering.
Renal impairment increases need for careful fluid balance, rasburicase consideration, and dialysis backup.

side_effects.interpretation: Aggressive fluids can worsen pulmonary edema in vulnerable patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Metabolic protection vector that prevents TLS from translating into AKI, arrhythmia, seizure, and mortality.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Product availability, antibodies, volume tolerance, or transfusion reaction risk can limit support.
Bleeding pressure increases value of platelet/RBC/fibrinogen support.

side_effects.interpretation: Volume overload or transfusion lung injury can worsen respiratory status.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supportive vector that improves oxygen delivery and reduces bleeding event hazards without treating leukemia burden.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Febrile neutropenia creates high pre-test probability of dangerous infection.
Documented or suspected infection strengthens antimicrobial effect on sepsis hazard.

side_effects.interpretation: Some antimicrobials can worsen kidney function.
Antimicrobial hepatotoxicity or interactions can constrain therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supportive infection vector that prevents neutropenic fever from progressing into sepsis and death.

supportive_care: Use presentation-time CBC with differential, smear blast fraction, vitals, fever history, pain, lymph node/hepatosplenic exam, organ function labs, LDH, uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium, bilirubin fractions, coagulation and infection workup as ordinary observations.
Keep marrow morphology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics, molecular findings, CSF cytology/flow, and tissue pathology as confirmatory or treatment-context evidence rather than ordinary ranking evidence.
Monitor hyperleukocytosis for CNS, retinal, pulmonary, renal, and cardiac leukostasis; capture symptoms and organ findings without requiring confirmatory marrow evidence for ranking.
Treat tumor lysis risk as an event-hazard chain with hydration, urate lowering, electrolyte monitoring, and dialysis backup rather than as a black-box mortality penalty.

Preserve hepatic/biliary infiltration presentations: jaundice, bilirubin fractions, ALP/GGT, hepatomegaly, imaging, and biopsy context should not be deleted even if they mimic cholangitis or hepatitis.

Trend blood counts and use RBC/platelet support, infection prophylaxis/treatment, and neutropenic fever protocols as supportive vector fields while definitive leukemia-directed therapy reshapes disease burden.
